correctness.rationale: The universal signature bound 2^m-1≥16 gives m≥5. A representative Shrikhande five-code was checked by its 16 nonempty distinct signatures; all 16·6 parity-coset/local-edge templates are valid, and every one of all C(16,5)=4368 candidate five-sets was independently tested, yielding exactly 96 and the same family. A single exchange preserves the unique three-member parity coset and its missing point, so each q-indexed component is the line graph of its six-neighbor C6, hence C6. In the rook graph independent closed-neighborhood signature enumeration over all subsets through size6 gives exactly 2208 minima; every pair differing by one code point was joined, yielding 28800 edges and a single component, and BFS from all 2208 states yielded eccentricity 6 each. Both supplied C++ and Python algorithms were inspected and independent Python recomputation reproduced the counts. This exhaustive finite proof has no generalization to larger Doob graphs.

evidence: Gravier–Moncel–Semri Theorem 1 proves gamma_ID(K_n□K_n)=floor(3n/2), so the rook minimum size6 is already known; for even n it mentions multiple types of codes but not a complete exchange census. originality.rationale: Gravier–Moncel–Semri 2008 Theorem 1 already proves rook minimum size floor(3n/2), so n=4 gives 6 as known background (no claimed new gamma_ID(R)). Their even-n construction and optimal-size theorem do not enumerate 2208 labelled minima or optimum replacement connectivity. Gravier et al. 2015 discuss vertex-transitive and strongly regular identifying codes and recall Cartesian clique products, but explicitly note few known optimal SRG cases; the inspected material lacks this Shrikhande classification and both exchange graphs. Prior homology distinctions for this SRG pair in Resultary use a different invariant, not these code signatures.
residual_risks: An unindexed published computer enumeration of Shrikhande/rook identifying codes might contain the 96/2208 exchange graphs.
Rook optimal size6 belongs to Gravier–Moncel–Semri (2008), and is explicitly not a novel finding.
Scope is two specific 16-vertex graphs; optimal codes may be connected if temporary larger code sizes are allowed, not covered here.

value.rationale: Identifying-code minima are standard sensor placement quantities. A graph with only 16 vertices that meets the sharp information-theoretic size bound, and the contrast between disconnected and connected optimum-preserving sensor exchange despite identical SRG(16,6,2,2) parameters, form a natural and nontrivial geometric classification, not an unmotivated arbitrary graph census.

final_claim: The Shrikhande graph has exactly 96 minimum closed-neighborhood identifying codes of size 5, geometrically classified by a missing parity-coset point and an edge of its local C6, with exchange graph 16 disjoint C6; the 4x4 rook graph has 2208 minimum codes of known size 6 and a connected 28800-edge optimum-exchange graph of diameter/radius 6.
limitations: Exact finite result for S and K4□K4, closed-neighborhood signatures, fixed-cardinality single-site swaps.
No claim about all SRGs(16,6,2,2) beyond these two isomorphism types, or general Doob graphs.
